newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-T-bonds fail to spark interest near highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-T-bonds fail to spark interest near highs.

text.p: U.S. debt futures dipped slightly, as June T-bonds failed to spark momentum at the upper end of one-and-a-half month ranges.
"Overall, the tone is constructive, but gains got ahead of themselves," David Ging, Treasury market strategist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, said about Friday's rally.

June T-bonds rose near the overnight high of 110-04/32, but are not expected to test the one-and-a-half month high of 110-10/32 before the U.S. Federal Reserve releases its Beige Book on Wednesday afternoon, technical analysts said.
Ging said the two-month high of 110-14/32 would cap the market on the upside.
In fact, some questioned the likelihood of June T-bonds testing 110-08/32, a level that corresponded to a U.S. long bond yield of 6.87 percent on Friday.
One trader said the 6.87 percent level was significant because the cash bond was trading at level, or 109-25/32 in June T-bonds, when the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) raised rates in March.
"I think we will spin our wheels between 110-08/32 and 108-18/32 between now and FOMC on May 20," one source said.
The 108-18/32 level currently corresponds to a long bond yield of 7.00 percent.
Several technicians said the market which had set a seven-and-a-half month low of 106-12/32 on April 11 was oversold, and that weekly momentum indicators had gradually turned higher.
However, they said the market would set a long-term bottom in the summer months.
"We've had a bottom, but I don't think it's the bottom," Bruce Kamich, senior vice president at MCM Moneywatch, said.
Kamich said candlestick chart patterns indicate bearish price action in both T-bonds and Eurodollars.
"Even though they had a big range on Friday, Eurodollars closed where they opened," he said. "It really marks indecision after Friday's rally and leaves Friday's buyers under water."
While June T-bonds closed at a seven-month high settlement at 109-29/32, the close was only 06/32 higher from where the contract opened.
"For all their efforts they could only push it up by six," he said.
